title: Host Web Apps with App Service

questions.prompt: What is the relationship between an App Service plan and a web app?

options.text: They are two names for the same thing
The plan is the compute; the web app runs inside it, and several apps can share a plan
The web app is the compute; the plan runs inside the app
A plan can hold only one web app, ever

questions.explanation: The App Service plan provides the compute (region, OS, size, tier); web apps run inside it, and multiple apps can share one plan.

questions.prompt: Which statements about App Service are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Scaling up means moving to a bigger plan; scaling out means more instances
Autoscale and deployment slots require Standard tier or higher
A managed certificate can provide free HTTPS on a custom domain
You must patch the underlying OS yourself

questions.explanation: Scale up = bigger, scale out = more instances; autoscale/slots need Standard+; managed certificates give free TLS. App Service is PaaS, so Azure patches the OS.

questions.prompt: A live copy of a web app (like 'staging') that you can swap into production for a zero-downtime release is a deployment ____.
questions.explanation: Deployment slots (Standard+) let you deploy and test in staging, then swap into production near-instantly, with an easy swap-back to roll back.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of a zero-downtime release using slots.

items.text: Deploy the new version to the staging slot

questions.explanation: Deploy to staging, test there, then swap into production; if there's a problem, swap back to roll back.

questions.prompt: Match each App Service term to its meaning.

pairs.right: A swappable live copy like staging

questions.explanation: The plan is the compute; scale up = bigger; scale out = more instances; a slot is a swappable copy.
